facts.raw_span: painful swelling of the calves
no evidence of deep venous thrombosis or soft-tissue infection
elevated LDH and CK
negative autoimmune serology
CT scan showed no lymphoma relapse but diffuse subcutaneous edema
elevated CRP, transaminases, CK, troponin I, myoglobin, and LDH
reduced plasma protein, albumin, and IgG
MRI of the thighs showed diffuse intramuscular and extramuscular edema
muscle biopsy demonstrated interstitial and perivascular T-cell and macrophage infiltrates
acute kidney injury secondary to rhabdomyolysis
Cardiac MRI confirmed myocarditis
CSF analysis showed leukocyte count 329/μl, lactate 3.5 mmol/L, and protein 79.6 mg/dl

concepts.why: Elevated CK and muscle biopsy demonstrating interstitial and perivascular T-cell and macrophage infiltrates support the diagnosis of polymyositis.
Cardiac MRI confirmation of myocarditis supports this diagnosis.
Acute kidney injury secondary to rhabdomyolysis supports this diagnosis.

aliases: Inflammatory Disease of the Spinal Cord
concepts.why: CSF analysis and spinal MRI findings support the diagnosis of myelitis.

rationales.F01: Painful swelling of the calves could indicate muscle inflammation, suggesting polymyositis.
rationales.F03: Elevated LDH and CK are indicative of muscle damage, which could be due to polymyositis or rhabdomyolysis.
rationales.F06: Elevated CRP, transaminases, CK, troponin I, myoglobin, and LDH suggest widespread inflammation and muscle damage, indicating polymyositis, myocarditis, or rhabdomyolysis.
rationales.F08: Diffuse intramuscular and extramuscular edema on MRI suggests muscle inflammation, consistent with polymyositis or rhabdomyolysis.
rationales.F09: Muscle biopsy demonstrating interstitial and perivascular T-cell and macrophage infiltrates is highly suggestive of polymyositis.
rationales.F10: Acute kidney injury secondary to rhabdomyolysis indicates severe muscle damage, consistent with rhabdomyolysis.
rationales.F11: Cardiac MRI confirmation of myocarditis indicates inflammation of the heart muscle, consistent with myocarditis.
rationales.F12: CSF analysis showing elevated leukocyte count, lactate, and protein suggests inflammation of the spinal cord, consistent with myelitis.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's presentation with painful swelling of the calves, elevated LDH and CK, and muscle biopsy demonstrating interstitial and perivascular T-cell and macrophage infiltrates strongly supports polymyositis, which is further complicated by myocarditis as evidenced by cardiac MRI confirmation.
